claim: "vendor claims of 28-50% incident reductions are unattributed to a specific deployment with a control group" (measured_outcomes, last row, citing the Smartvid.io PRNewswire release)
problem: The cited release only supports the 50% figure ("cut incident rates by as much as 50 percent for some of the world's largest construction companies"). The 28% end of the range does not appear on the cited page; it circulates in vendor/case-study material elsewhere (e.g. a Smartvid/Newmetrix claim of a 28% recordable-rate reduction) and is not sourced in this row.
fix: Either cite the specific source for the 28% figure, or narrow the row to "vendor claims of up to ~50% reductions (e.g. Smartvid.io PRNewswire, Dec 2020)".

claim: The NIBRS construction-theft study (ETSUniversity Pure record, "An Exploratory Look at Thefts from Construction Sites") is labeled study_type "peer-reviewed" in both problem.evidence and measured_outcomes.
problem: The record shows the item as a conference paper presented at the Annual Associated Schools of Construction International Conference (10 April 2019), i.e. conference proceedings, not a peer-reviewed journal article. The numbers themselves ($6,000 average, $42,000 trucks, 55% truck recovery, under 7% overall recovery, 15,000+ incidents) are all confirmed on the page.
fix: Relabel study_type as "conference proceedings" (strength can stay Medium).

claim: Efficient-YOLOv5 harness detector dated "2022" (measured_outcomes row 2, DOI 10.1049/ipr2.12696).
problem: Wiley/DOAJ record the article as Xu, IET Image Processing, 2023 (some citing papers give 2022 for the online version). The metrics (97.7% precision, 89.3% recall, 94% mAP, dataset of 3,300 images) are confirmed, but the year is ambiguous.
fix: Write "2022/2023 (online 2022, IET Image Processing 17)" or use 2023.

problem: The Evercam price list shows $500/month for the Software Service (TLC Package) as a package price, plus $500/month for each "Additional Fixed Position Camera" and $800/month for an additional PTZ. "Per camera" is an inference about effective cost, not the page's wording.
fix: Say "$500/month software service, plus $500/month for each additional fixed camera", or label the per-camera framing as an inference.

claim: TrueLook jobsite-security survey dated "2020" (739 respondents, 78% reported theft).
problem: The article page carries no publication date; the 2020 attribution appears only in the embedded report image alt text ("TrueLook Jobsite Security Report 2020") and the page is hosted under a 2026 upload path. Respondent count and 78% are confirmed.
fix: Note "survey report dated 2020 per the report artwork; article page undated".

claim: Discrepancy note between the two BLS releases mentions only the count (421 vs 423).
problem: The TED page also states 38.5% of construction deaths were falls, slips and trips, while the CFOI release says 39.2% (421). The count note is correct but incomplete; a reader comparing the two pages will also meet the percentage gap.
fix: Extend the note to mention 38.5% (TED) vs 39.2% (CFOI) so the 39.2% figure used in fit_score is not read as inconsistent.

claim: Caveats say the 29 CFR 1904.1 small-employer exemption and 1904.39 reporting deadlines "were not read at source" (osha.gov 403).
problem: Both rules are readable and accurate at a non-OSHA copy (law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/29/1904.1 and 1904.39): exemption is company-wide 10-or-fewer in the prior calendar year, reporting duties survive, and 8-hour fatality / 24-hour in-patient-hospitalization, amputation or eye-loss deadlines are exactly as stated. This is a sourcing understatement, not an error.
fix: Upgrade both to confirmed with the LII/eCFR mirror as the citation.
